incident_description:
Caller's daughter purchased a GE range approximately 18 months ago.

They are having problems with the knobs on her gas range which turn on very easily.

The caller is reporting that if a person just rubs past or is reaching over the range the knobs turn at times and begin releasing gas but do not ignite.

He said that this has happened a few times and that just recently the dog walker came into the home and smelled gas then turn it off.

There are no known injuries at this time 

The caller contacted the manufacturer on December 4th, 2014 and he was advised that a service technician would be sent to the home December 9th, 2014.

The caller will update this report with the technician's statements before he returns it.

1.  At 1:30 on Dec 9th G.E. Technician ([REDACTED] stopped by the caller's daughter's residence, the caller explained to him the problem.  He operated several of the knobs on the range.  He said without hesitation that there was nothing he could do about it, that it was a problem with the design of the knobs. 

The caller asked if there was anyone else the callers could talk to in order to resolve the problem?

He said he would let someone know and punched some info into his computer.  As he was leaving at 1:37 the caller requested that someone call her on the following day with a way to rectify this safety issue.  He said he would let someone know.  (No reply from G.E. on following day)

2.  At 1:45 on Dec 9th the caller called [REDACTED] at Customer Service (800-386-1215 ext. #[REDACTED]) to let him know that the Technician had been here and what he had said.  (Voice message (He would call her back in 24 to 48 hours

3.  At 1:19 on Dec 10th [REDACTED] called the caller back and said there was nothing that he could do but offer the callers a new range at our expense and they would pickup the old one and probably scrap it or he could send another Tech. for a second opinion.  The caller told him none of the options would solve this issue since the caller was aware of at least 5 other consumers with the same identical problem

As a final note he said the caller could go on line to see if anything could be done (GECHSconsumers@GE.com

4.  Dec. 12th 12:23 Called GE Corporate HQTRS. in Fairfield Connecticut #203-373-2211.  Message prompter sent caller back to Consumer Complaint Dept. (which she had already been to!)

Dec. 12th 12:30 Called G.E. Corporate Offices.  Left message that she had an issue of safety about one of their ranges and needed to talk to someone who could help.

Dec. 12th 5:05 PM.  Operator called back with number for CEO in charge of appliances.

Dec 13th 12:40  Called CEO [REDACTED] [REDACTED]  He said he had checked the report from the technician and confirmed what the Tech. said.  The caller asked him if he knew of any other complaints about this issue.  He said that he had heard of people accidently turning on the gas while reaching over the range to access a microwave or cabinet above range.  So the caller asked if he knew he was acknowledging that there was a problem with the range.  He said no that he had only heard of such issues .  The caller asked if there was some other dept. or person in engineering or product safety that she could talk to about this.  He said there was nothing more he could do.

The caller was thoroughly amazed and disgusted with the cavalier additude with which he approached this problem, so she informed him that she would take another approach  but that this issue was too serious to just let it go!!

P.S.  Enclosed: At least 5 other consumers with the identical issue.

Thank you!
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a gas leak due to easily turned knobs, posing a safety hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
The front left burner was in use, when the glass top shattered.  The burner had been in use for approx. 7 minutes, on the setting of 8.  The consumer turned the burner off and moved the pan over to one of the burners that had not been in use.  The glass shattered within 1 - 2 minutes of the consumer turning it off.  He also noted that instead of the burner becoming more dim, when he turned it off, it seemed to be getting hotter.  The consumer believes that he was not injured, because he had moved several feet away from the range at the time of the incident.  However, he believes that if someone were closer, they could have been injured.

Most of the glass dropped down on top of the range, but the consumer later found pieces of glass on the floor.  The broken glass varied in size.  Initially the consumer thought that the glass mainly broke over the burner that had been in use, but he noticed cracks through other parts of the glass.  

2/3/2016:  The consumer called Frigidaire and their rep. (name unknown) filed an incident report:  [REDACTED].  The consumer said that he had to ask for the report number, because the firm did not willingly provide it to him. The consumer said that the rep. indicated that he had the range for 10 years and they tried to sell him a warranty, which he declined.

2/3/2016:  The consumer also called the retailer, but their rep. indicated that the range was out of warranty and did not offer any other assistance.  The consumer told the rep. that he never liked the range, because he could not clean it to his satisfaction.  The rep. said that he never cleaned it, but he corrected her and reiterated that he couldnt clean it as well as he preferred.
  
For the first couple of years the consumer used the range daily, but over the last 2 - 3 years, they only use it a few times a week.

In the first couple weeks he owned the range, when he turned the range on, the display panel did not indicate the correct temperature.  This was either the front or rear right burner, but the consumer cant remember exactly which burner.  It was repaired under warranty and an authorized technician replaced one of the burners.  This enabled the consumer to view the burner settings correctly.

NOTE:  The consumer said that the mfr's rep. cross-referenced his range under the brand name Crosley, but he did not see that name anywhere on his range.

The beginning model numbers of the consumer's range appear to match the ones in CAP# 09-333.


The consumer looked on the Internet and when he typed Frigidaire exploding electric range, he saw numerous other reports.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer again after he found a recall on the Internet.  The manufacturer said the switches need to be replaced.  They offered to send the consumer a switch.  He would have to get a service person.  He told them the range was destroyed when the glass exploded.  They said the recall was for the switch.
justification: The glass top shattered but no injury occurred, though potential for injury was noted if someone was closer.

incident_description:
Danby propane refrigerator being used at a cabin.  Refrigerator was operational for approximately 2 years.  It began to emit carbon monoxide into the cabin killing my 10 year old son, and nearly killing my wife and 8 year old daughter.
The refrigerator uses propane as an energy source to operate the refrigeration cycle.  the burner uses a small flame a little bigger than a candle.  We had done light maintenance on the unit, but it seems that in the course of running out of propane a few times the burner started to create soot.  A piece of soot fell down onto the top of the burner, causing it to burn incorrectly and emit CO.  
The unit is certified to operate inside an occupied residence.  The design is such that it does not require flue gas venting to the exterior.  There are no safety devises to shut the unit down or alert the occupants if the flame begins to burn incorrectly, as in my case.
We have found that there have been 20 or more deaths linked to propane refrigerators in Canada, and that Canada requires the unit to come with a CO detector.  This is not a requirement in the united states.  
There is a state of [REDACTED] police report as well as media reports on the incident.
I did not have a CO detector installed in the cabin.  If I had one, it is very likely this incident would have been avoided.
justification: The incident resulted in a death and near-fatal injuries, indicating high severity. The occurrence likelihood is considered possible due to the reported cases and lack of safety devices.

incident_description:
This following incident occurred with a GE Profile dishwasher MN: PDW7700G00WW and SN: VA774228B.

The incident below is particularly concerning because it appears to be an identical fault described in a GE recall number 12-244 issued August 9, 2012 but my unit is not covered.  This recall pertains to the same model number as my unit but the serial number of my unit eliminates it from the existing recall. 

Approximately two hours after completing a dishwashing cycle I was alerted to the smell of burning plastic coming from the dishwasher. The dishwasher indicated that it was off but the front panel was extremely hot. After opening the door an I received burns on my arm from the extreme hot air that was escaping.  Nearly all plastic dishes had either completely melted and fell onto direct contact with the heating element or were severely deformed.  No front panel controls would result in the heating element from shutting off.  Only turning off the circuit breaker to the dishwasher allowed the heating element to shut off.  If nobody was present in the home when this fault occurred it would have undoubtedly resulted in a fire. 

With the dishwasher in service mode I was able to repeatedly initiate the fault by switching the heating element on.  It appears that once the heating element is switched on it will not turn off until power is removed via a circuit breaker.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the arm and potential fire hazard, indicating injury severity (level 3). The fault is reproducible, suggesting a likely occurrence (level 4).

incident_description: (8/1/2024) The consumer has a safety concern about her LG range. She stated that the front left burner will not go out at times. Also, about a year ago there was a spillover on top of the stove. Some of the spillover went under the cook top. The cooktop doesn't seem to be sealed properly.
justification: The burner not turning off and spillover under the cooktop pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The range oven turns on by itself.  It appears to be in the clean mode.  It will not shut off on it's own.  The circuit breaker must be turned off or the system unplugged.  We were lucky to be home when this has happened.
justification: The oven turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported in this instance.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung double oven model:NX60A6751SS over the summer. This particular oven has a removable piece inside that allows it to be used as a double oven or single oven if the piece is removed. The first time I tried using it, the food I had in the top oven immediately started to burn. Luckily I smelled it right away and removed it. I assumed I had done something wrong. The next time I used it, I preheated the oven and placed a dish inside. Not long after, I was in another room and smelled smoke. There was a fire inside my oven! Thank God I smelled it. I got it put out before it spread. After weeks and weeks of going through trouble-shooting and such, I realized that they use a broiler to heat the top oven. Even if you put the oven on "bake" it uses a broiler which burns and causes fire to anything you place inside. Samsung sends repair people out to fix it but they cannot do anything because that is the design of the oven. After multiple small fires, I can now only use the tiny bottom portion of the oven or I risk the lives of my family. This product should not ever have been placed on the market. I have personally read hundreds of reviews online of the same exact story as mine.
justification: The incident involved multiple small fires but no injuries or deaths, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to numerous similar reports and the inherent design flaw.

incident_description: My 1yr old Kenmore dishwasher overheated and caught fire from the control board and soap dispenser.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: The consumer stated that the smoke was coming from the door of the dishwasher on 09/09/2020. The consumer shut the unit off at the circuit breaker and thought it was cut off. When the unit started smoking again, the consumer discovered  that it was connected to a different breaker box.  The entire unit was extremely hot as well as the counter on top of the unit.
justification: The incident involved smoke and overheating but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Consumer was using microwave to melt butter.  Unit started arcing, making a sound like an electrocution.  Butter in dish caught fire
justification: The microwave arcing and butter catching fire is an incident with potential for injury but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Frigidaire cooktop which I bought new in March of 2008 started getting stuck on high heat no matter which setting it was on. I would be able to just turn it off. Then it started sticking on high and I was not able to get it to shut off at all unless I turned the breaker off. I looked online to see if there were similar problems to mine. I found there was a recall on certain models for this very problem so I called Frigidaire but was told my cooktop was not among the ones under recall even though mine is doing the very thing the others were being recalled for. Evidently this is a recurring problem but they are not willing to stand behind their product. I am very disappointed in them and will not buy another Frigidaire product. I believe this to be a very serious problem on a cooktop that is not that old!
justification: The cooktop malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, only inconvenience and dissatisfaction.

incident_description:
Mfg / Supplier Swedausa.com
ASI # 90305
Coffee Mug
The above mentioned product should be recalled immediately.  It has the look & feel of any other type of coffee mug, however, the internal note states:
USE:
Hot liquids are not recommended
If this "coffee mug looking" container is not recommended for hot liquids, than what was it designed for?
justification: The product is misleading and not suitable for its intended use, but no injury or incident is reported.

incident_description: The consumer says the burner turn on by themselves or will not turn off.  the knob says it is in the off position and still be turned on.  The consumer also says that while in use the temperature will fluctuate without her adjusting the temperature.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer today  who offered to schedule an appointment for a fee.  The consumer says at first it was only the front right burner that was acting up.  the consumer is having the same issues as listed in Release # 09-333.  Her model number is not listed in the recall.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a potential safety hazard but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
A couple of days ago while using the oven on our Kenmore stove, we noticed it was smoking a lot.  We opened the door and it seemed like the temperature was much higher than normal (it was set to 400 degrees) yet the lower element was glowing orange.  We turned off the oven via the control panel, and the display responded as if the oven had been turned off (the temperature display disappeared) but the element kept glowing orange.  Also there's usually a "click" when the oven cycles on or off and we did not hear that when we shut off the oven.

After a couple of minutes, the element was still bright orange and it was obvious that the oven had not actually shut off.  I went downstairs and shut off the circuit breaker for the stove and only then did the element start to cool.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but was successfully turned off via the circuit breaker, preventing injury or further damage.

incident_description: GE Dishwasher model PDT750SSF5SS had electrical wiring issue which caused an electrical fire during a normal cycle with a small dishwashing load. Model not currently recalled. The smell was noticed and the fire caught early, so damage is only to appliance.
justification: Electrical fire caused damage to the appliance but was caught early with no injuries.

incident_description: I have a GE Microwave only two years old. When cooking, sparks and fire shoots from the top right side of the inner panel. I did a [REDACTED] search and determined this is a common problem with GE Microwave. The Model Number is JES1290SK 02. Have you had other complaints and what can I do as a consumer?
justification: The description reports sparks and fire, indicating an incident with potential for harm but no actual injury mentioned.

incident_description: After cooking cupcakes, our Kenmore Electric Range (model # 790-942-234-00) oven door shattered sending tiny glass pieces all over our kitchen.
justification: The oven door shattered, causing glass pieces to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Our Kenmore Dishwasher suddenly started smoking, sparking and smelled of burnt plastic.  We shut it off and hit the electrical breaker as well as unplugged it.  This is the second dishwasher from Sears that has started on fire.  The first one was a [REDACTED] purchased before 2004.
justification: The dishwasher caused a fire hazard (smoking, sparking), but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The issues I am having with my Samsung refrigerator is the temperature control within the unit is warmer than the controls on the refrigerator is indicating. The unit is at the point where food is spoiling, and we are eating unsafe food. We are also experiencing problems with the ice maker. It is freezing up. It needs to be defrosted once a week and even still it does not produce ice as it should. We originally exchanged the unit back in 2016 because we believed we had a lemon unit. Come to find that this model of Samsung refrigerator is a defect.
justification: The refrigerator's temperature control issues and ice maker problems are causing food spoilage and potential health risks, but no direct injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I was not using the product at the time of occurrence. I have a Samsung stove that I do not know make and model of at the moment. 
I had made eggs earlier in the day. As I took a pot of the stove not touching the knobs or burners. A burner that did not have the pot on it decided to start. It kept trying to turn on and I could hear the clicking as if it was trying to turn on for gas stove. All the knobs were off as I checked. I did not know how to turn off so I called 911 and the fire dept came and turned the gas off to the stove. Im just thankful I was awake and not sleeping when it decided to turn on. I cannot emphasize enough that I did not touch the burner that came on.
justification: The incident involved a stove malfunctioning and turning on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I am reporting a serious safety hazard involving a Whirlpool gas cooktop, model WCG51US6DS00. The units grates are unstable and slip out of place. In one incident, a grate slipped and struck the control knobs, turning on a burner without my knowledge. This caused gas to fill my house, creating a severe risk of fire, explosion, or poisoning. The knobs are also loose and broken, compounding the danger.The grates on this unit are unstable and do not stay in place. One incident caused a grate to slip, strike the control knobs, and accidentally turn on a burner. This left gas flowing into the house undetected, creating a severe fire, explosion, and poisoning hazard. The knobs are also loose and broken, increasing the risk. Whirlpool customer support acknowledged the issue (ticket # [REDACTED]) but refused to provide a remedy beyond offering a 20% discount on a new appliance, which does not address the existing hazard. This product poses a serious risk and should be investigated for recall.
justification: The unstable grates and loose knobs caused gas to leak, posing severe fire, explosion, and poisoning risks, though no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: On July 16, 2014, my LG refrigerator, model LFX21960**, purchased on Sept. 14, 2006 had failed to turn off the lights even though the doors were closed. This melted the inside top of refrigerator lining and the plastic light covering. Due to the heat of the bulbs which were still incredibly hot, he internal temperature was much warmer than it should have been.
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore model #790.92803011 glass door exploded when I open it. I was pre heating the oven and then opened the door and it popped and the glass door shattered everywhere. What a mess and glass pieces in fingers. Sears in my area will be no help because the one year warranty is over. The stove is 1 1/2 and now I am left with an ugly looking door unless I want to pay $239 to replace. This incident could have been much worst this product should really be on a recall list as this is a hazard.
justification: Glass pieces caused minor injury (glass in fingers), but no severe harm occurred.

incident_description: My GE gas range stove plastic valve knob strips and no longer indicates the true position of the gas valve, as a result the stove has been left on, gas with no flame and gas with flame. As  a result the smoke alarms activated alerting us to the danger.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a faulty valve knob, leading to smoke alarm activation but no injury or death.

incident_description: My daughter plugged in our new Chefman Air Fryer my wife got for Christmas to cook some French fries. As it was warming up my wife heard a popping noise in the kitchen ran in to see and saw the air fryer had caught fire underneath from the power cord and burned out counter top.
justification: The air fryer caught fire and burned the countertop, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We had a Panasonic model NN-SB65NS microwave delivered to our house by Walmart. It was kept on a counter top, minimaly used, and just under three months old. 

Our twelve year old son attempted to make a bag of popcorn using the popcorn setting and the inside began to spark and smoke. He screamed for help and we came to his aid. The popcorn was on fire at this point and our kitchen had filled with smoke. After contacting support we do not feel the seriousness of the sparking issue is understood or believed. Pictures, info and receipt were sent and the unit is bagged. 

I have been clear stating I am unable to ship the microwave to Panasonic Engineers to study. It was delivered for a reason. As you will see from the attached email screenshots, the incident will be closed if they are not sent the microwave carefully packaged. I do understand why this is important. It is also extremely important that consumers are kept safe and not belittled by corporations.
While I don't expect a refund anymore as I physically cannot lift their burned microwave. I expect the issue to be documented.

UPDATED ON 6/18/2025: [Our microwave sparked from the interior plate to the point the popcorn caught on fire. My 12yo was screaming for help, unplugged the unit, and singed his fingers on the microwave.

We have been belittled by Panasonic customer service and emailed by a legal representative who assumes our situation is not true and will delete the info if we don't send the unit back. However, we are disabled and had the unit delivered and set up. 

We are not asking for a refund. Only that this is investigated and nobody else goes through this. ]
justification: The incident involved a microwave sparking and causing a fire, with the 12-year-old sustaining singed fingers, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he has an electric range that the surface heating elements change
Spontaneously. The consumer stated that all of the burner had been experiencing the same problems, but the front burners have been experiencing more problems. The consumer stated that after turning the knobs to off, the burners continued to be on. The consumer had to turn off the circuit breaker to turn the range off. 
The consumer stated that when he turn the knobs to off, the range lights show that the elements are off, but that the hot surface light stays on. He stated that the burners do not turn off. 
The consumer stated that no one was injured. The consumer stated that there were no damages to his home structure. 
The consumer believes that his range was experiencing the same hazard stated on release # 09-333.
The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that there was no
recall on his particular model.

UPDATE: One thing that has not been included in this report is that on the evening after I made the report, the range actually caught on fire.  We have a family of five and we were trying to get by by turning the circuit  breaker back on only when we needed to cook.  I turned the breaker back on and was cooking on the manfunctioning burner (since it was staying on anyway), and something below the control panel and behind the range top started glowing red.  When the burner cut off and back on (to regulate the burner temperature), a loud pop occured and fire shot from under the control panel across the room. I turned the breaker off permanently and have not tried to use the range since.  Trying to use this type of range once you have noticed problems could lead to a house fire.  I would recommend to anyone not to use this product once problems have been discovered.

My family and I have owned several Kenmore products over the years with no complaints.  Since this report, I have ordered a new Kenmore gas range/oven and a matching Kenmore microwave (model #s 72903 and 85033).  I have faith in Kenmore products and hope they will do what is right in regards to the problems I had.  Our new oven and microwave is to be delivered on 8/3/12.  This is the earliest I could get one and have been without a range/oven since 7/10/12, which has been a big inconvenience.
justification: The range malfunctioned and caught fire, but no injuries or structural damages were reported.

incident_description:
(04/2016) The consumer stated that the knobs on the range cracked on the inside. The consumer was not able to turn off the burners properly . Also this caused gas leaks.

The consumer contacted LG who sent courtesy replacement knobs.

About six months later, one by one the knobs began to crack again. 

(09/13/2017) The consumer contacted LG again and sent pictures. The consumer was advised that there is nothing that can be done. They also advised her that they had already sent courtesy replacements knobs. The consumer was referred to the parts departments to purchase new knobs.

The consumer stated that this is a safety issue.
justification: The incident involved cracked knobs causing gas leaks, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I just visited the Consumer Product Safety Commission concerning a problem with a GE Profile dishwasher.
The product recall number is 12-244 which list several models of the GE dishwashers with the prefix for the model number and serial numbers. Although our GE Profile model number or serial number is not listed we still had a problem. Our model number is PDWF800R10BB and serial number is DT718621B and was purchased during the time frame listed on the recall. Recently the dishwasher was running and we heard a loud pop. When I checked the circuit breaker was tripped and the plug, where the dish washer was connected was burned and melted. I had the plug replaced and reconnected the dishwasher and it seems to work with the exception of the heating element. We have two of the GE Profile dishwashers purchased approximately the same time period. After reading the report I now have concerns as to the safety of the units. The only reason I came across the recall was because I was checking out replacement heating elements.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing a circuit breaker to trip and a plug to melt, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: GE Profile glass oven door shattered the first time I used the oven. New oven was installed 05/16/24 and the oven door glass exploded on 05/17/24.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Bosch dishwasher model SHU43C05UC installed in 2004.  Machine was running through wash cycles when area behind cycle selection buttons on front of machine apparently shorted out and caused a fire.  I turned off the electricity and the fire continued to burn and grow.  Tried to blow out the fire with breath,  When that didn't work tried to smother fire with a wet cloth. When that didn't kill the fire I had to use a dry chemical fire extinguisher to put out the fire.  The selection buttons and the surrounding plastic enclosure were melted and burned.  The flames went up and under the wood counter base.  Had we not been near the dishwasher the flames would have ignited the counter and then the wood cabinets on both sides resulting in a major fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have escalated but was contained without injury or death.

incident_description: Shortly after starting the dishwasher the control panel starting smoking and had flames coming out. I attempted to shut the power off at the control panel as I called 911. It would not shut off so I had to flip the circuit breaker off. The flames and smoke started to decrease so I asked the dispatcher if the fire department still needed to respond. I was told that yes they did. They have all the info on make, model and what damage was done I their report.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Oven glass blew out
justification: The oven glass blowing out is an incident with potential for injury but none was reported in the description.

incident_description: The through the door ice dispenser on a [REDACTED] refrigerator drops ice onto the floor after dispensing ice into a glass. Recently on date below, over an hour passed when a cube fell onto the floor presenting a slipping hazard.  Ice drops out frequently usually after only a few minutes, but nearly every week.  Model number[REDACTED]
justification: Ice falling on the floor presents a slipping hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Microwave would start running when the door was opened. I called West Bend about the situation on 05/12/2015 and was told told to get rid of it and buy a new one. West Bend: Model # EM925AJW-P2, FCC ID: RSFXM925AYY, Date Code 1319

Wife opened microwave after timer rang, opened door wheel continued to turn and coffee was moving around on glass turntable. Could still hear microwaves,  While only few seconds she reached in quickly to grab coffee cup and was slightly burned on hand and lower wrist and arm by microwaves.  Skin was only lightly reddened on skin, did not require ER trip.  After slight reddening went away still had sensation of being burnt. Did go away.
justification: The incident resulted in a slight burn, indicating an injury (severity 3), and the malfunction suggests a possible recurrence if the microwave is not replaced.

incident_description: Using the Mueller Austria Onion Choppers at the moment of trying to open the locking tab one finger slide to the blades and case a deep laceration.
justification: The description mentions a deep laceration, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Had on several occasions in recent months found microwave to be very warm when  not in use (including no lights or fan on). I could find no explanation for this.

I came downstairs at 6am last week and found the microwave running. It had self-started!  I do not know how long it had been running but it was extremely hot.    Unplugged the microwave and searched online for recalls or similar problems.  Found a number of blogs with similar complaints about this model.

I subsequently plugged in the microwave to use it  and after use did not unplug it but watched it closely.   After a few hours it randomly beeped and then ultimately self started again.

I have unplugged it and have not used it since.
justification: The microwave self-starting poses a fire hazard but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
I had just cooked breakfast in a Cuisinart small skillet and took the final pancake out of the pan, then moved the pan further back on the stove. All of a sudden, I heard a loud 'pop' that sounded like a gunshot, and something hit me in
the shoulder. However, I had horrible pain in my ears, and was holding both ears due to the pain from the loud sound. I had immediate 'ringing' in the ears and a red mark on my shoulder where I had been 'hit.' I had no idea what had happened and started looking around the room to see what had happened. I spoke with my friend and she asked me to check the walls and windows for bullet holes. (It had been THAT LOUD.) Then she asked me to take a look at my pan. She had heard about a recall on pans that had parts that went flying while cooking. I looked, and sure enough, one of the rivet covers from the inside of the pan (that holds the handle in place) was missing. I could not find it anywhere, though. I immediately called Cuisinart to discuss the incident with them. They had no resolution and said someone would call me back in 2-3 days. They did not call back; About an hour after my call, I was walking through my living room and found the rivet cover that had flown off the pan. It had traveled over 15 feet from the stove to its resting place in the living room.
justification: The incident caused pain in the ears, ringing, and a red mark on the shoulder, indicating injury.

incident_description: Kenmore Microwave Model 790.80323310 has created a fired hazard during operating use.  While operating microwave makes a cracking noise. Before replacing my microwave the first time; after the cracking like noise the microwave produced sparks and a flame was produced. A fire extinguisher had to be used to put out the fire. The second time, sparking noises occurred and the microwave was turned off immediately to prevent another fire.
justification: The microwave produced sparks and a flame, requiring a fire extinguisher, indicating a fire hazard with potential for injury.

incident_description:
My wife made a small pot of coffee successfully but before removing pot to fill cup was confronted with tremendous odor as though something was burning and/or melting. Didn't recognize source immediately but became bad enough to alarm children upstairs. Upon realizing coffee making was to blame, unplugged unit and burned hand trying to move off counter. Pot holder needed to remove unit outdoors. Very surprised counter top didn't melt. Warming plate beneath carafe was clearly so hot as to  melt unit's internals. Second unit to suffer similar fate. Good unit but not worth potential grievous injury.
Unit involved is Cuisinart programmable drip coffee maker perhaps 3 years old.  Whether it be 3 months or 5 years, I don't believe there ought be a time limit attached to consumer safety.
justification: The incident resulted in a burned hand, indicating an injury, and the description mentions this is the second occurrence with the same unit.

incident_description: Kenmore Microwave Oven model 665-6861191/ serial - XCJ1928012 Manufactured May 1999 caught fire 3/12/2011 at approx 10:45am while cooking a baked potatoe. Microwave had been on for approximately 3 minutes. Potatoe not overcooked.  Fire was put on immediately - Fireman came & ensured no further risk. Fireman cautioned that condominium had smoke but felt the cross winds of all open windows were sufficient to vent smoke without fans.
justification: Microwave caught fire but was extinguished immediately with no injuries reported.

incident_description: After using a veggetti vegetable slicer I bit something hard and I spit it out and it was a piece of metal that had broken off of the inside of the device.
justification: A piece of metal broke off the device but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore electric coil stove which is not a flat top.  Model #790.9421340G purchased in Nov. 2009.  The electric coils will burn on high even when the dial is set on low.  The elements need to be turned off to stop the burner from continueing on high.  The elements can be set on 5 and the next next minute the coil is red hot and out of control.  This happens everytime we use the stove and believe it is the same problem that the flat top stoves have.  It is very dangerous and extremely difficult to cook on this stove top.  I was told by sears to unplug it if I didn't feel safe, but that was all they could do without a service call.  I believe this is a safety recall issue and feel they are not acknowledging the problem with these coils and rotary switches.  I feel this model and other non flat top models with the digital display and rotary dials should be considered for addition to the recall list.  This is especially true if they are experiencing the same issues.  It cannot be ignored.  There are too many incident dates to include in the form below.  They simply won't fit.
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a burn and fire hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: I used an oven liner in my new oven during my first oven fryer use. There was a lot of smoke, which I attributed to the avacado oil. I learned afterward that it was the [REDACTED] coated oven liner that had apparently started smoking. My oven was left with a heavy white coating that doesnt come off completely. The [REDATED] was burned off the liner. I checked the item reviews again. (Amazon purchase) and found other reviews of this happening with fires occurring. I am personal concerned about the smoke I inhaled or that my family may have breathed. I think I may need to get rid of my oven and its two months old! Upon looking on the internet, it seems it has happened to a lot of people with other [REDACTED] coated liners.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential inhalation concerns, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I used my onion chopper and disassembled it to clean it with soap and water. After cleaning and drying it I attempted to put the grid blades back into its position within the chopper using my thumbs on too and my other fingers gripping the bottom. My left thumb slid onto the blades and severely cut it which prompted me to go to the emergency room as the wound profusely bled out. While at the hospital it continued to bleed for over 45 minutes. They could not use stitches because my thumb was mangled with multiple pieces of skin hanging off. I cant even pay for my medical bills from this stay at the ER even with insurance coverage.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring emergency room treatment, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I preheated the oven on my free standing electric range to 400 degrees and the inner glass panel shattered. The range is only 7 months old.
justification: The glass panel shattered but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Had set my LG Up/Down Oven in self clean mode. Soon after smoke was billowing throughout the house and was
woken by my son who lives across the road. Was overtaken by the smoke and home suffered smoke damage. The
product description Is as follows:
* LG Up/Down Oven
*Model#: LWD3010ST/00
* Product Code: LD3552SPASTLLGA
* S/N: 105SKMBVOT885
This is a very dangerous condition and could have taken my life, but for the actions of my son.
justification: The incident involved smoke inhalation and property damage, indicating injury and a hazardous condition.

incident_description: The Uncanny Brands R2-D2 Popcorn Maker is not properly designed. Hot popcorn and kernels fly out of it instead of going into a bowl. One of the kernels flew out at me and burned me in two spots on my chest. I had to carefully cleanup after running the machine to make sure I got every piece or popcorn or kernel that flew out so that my dog wouldnt eat it. It is not safe to use, especially around pets or small children.
justification: The incident resulted in burns from hot popcorn kernels, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this is a recurring issue with the product, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
I'm writing concerning my GE electric range, model #JB630DF4WW, that was purchased from Home Depot on 04-19-15. I did not purchase the extended warranty offered by Home Depot.  I have contacted GE and they are sending someone to check the damage.

On June 30, 2016, I was getting a glass pitcher out of the cabinet adjacent to my range.   The pitcher bumped the oven door and immediately the glass front fell to the floor at my feet.  The pitcher was not broken, so I know it was a slight bump.  Fortunately, I wasn't injured except for a small cut on my foot.  It only required minor first aid. The oven was last used four days prior to this incident.   I had never heard of this happening, but when checking on line, it appears this is not an isolated problem.

My concern is that mothers often have small children playing in the kitchen with pots, pans, wooden spoons, toys etc.  It seems very possible one of these objects could strike the range door causing the glass to break and injury a child or pet.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut requiring minor first aid, indicating an injury (severity 3). Online reports suggest this is not an isolated issue, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
While preheating my Kenmore oven this morning the outside glass blew out sending shards of glass across the floor. I looked online to see if others have had this problem and hundreds have reported the same issue to [REDACTED]. This is a serious issue! Had our grandchild been in the kitchen they could have had shards of glass blown into thier eyes. Fortunately I was able to pick the shards out of my legs and feet. 

Here is the link to [REDACTED] describing the issue. [REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused injury (shards in legs and feet) and potential for severe harm (glass in eyes), with multiple similar reports indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: GE microwave 2years old over oven $500.00.  Put potato in and in 2 minutes alarms went off and house filled with smoke.  Microwave completey burnt/melted
justification: The microwave caught fire and melted, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Wall oven glass door got so hot, I reflexively slammed the door shut after accidentally touching glass on outside of oven door, shattering the glass 

Extreme burn hazard for children!!!
justification: The incident involved a burn hazard and shattered glass, indicating potential for injury, especially to children.

incident_description:
My wife was baking a casserole using our kenmore smooth surface oven when we smelled something burning. Went to the kitchen to see smoke coming from the oven. I thought that I turned the stove off. I opened it up and my eyes started burning and to my amazement when I opened my eyes the element was still glowing red. I closed the door and pushed the oven buttom to off again.....thinking I missed it the first time I opened the door to get the casserole and the element was still on. I then told my wife to turn it off at the circuit breaker. I am sure if we were not upstair we would have had a fire and probably our pet would have died. 

our kenmore model # is 79095202103
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: (09/03/2024) This stove is unsafe for the public. It caught fire in my home. The fire burned my fingers and my feet. I was home with my family when it happened. I have pictures of the damages to my house and of my fingers and feet.
justification: The stove caught fire, causing burns to fingers and feet, which qualifies as an injury.
